name: Grumman G-21 Goose
summary: Eight-seat twin-radial amphibian built 1937–1945 for executives and the military; many still fly with piston or turboprop power in Alaska and the Caribbean.

wings: Straight high wing with large engines on the leading edge
Floats at or near the wingtips
engines: Two large round radial engines (some turboprop conversions)
fuselage: Deep, tall boat hull with a row of windows along the cabin
Main wheels fold up into the hull sides
tail: Single tall rounded fin and rudder

tellTales: Two radial engines on a high wing above a deep boat hull
Wheels that fold up into the sides of the hull
Floats near the wingtips on a large amphibian

confusedWith.howToTell: The Widgeon is much smaller with a stubby hull and a strut-braced tail; the Goose is bigger with large radial engines.
The Mallard is larger, with tricycle gear (nose wheel), wingtip tanks and a long row of square windows; the Goose has hull-mounted main wheels and no nose wheel.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
